correctness.rationale: The action t.[x:y]=[tx:y] is algebraic and preserves [x,y]=0 by bilinearity. If x and y are both nonzero, projective fixedness forces the compensating scalar simultaneously to equal t and 1, impossible for t!=1. Conversely the two coordinate projective subspaces are pointwise fixed and commute with zero. Thus the fixed locus is exactly two copies of P^{dim(g)-1}. Euler localization gives chi_c of the variety as chi_c of the fixed locus; projectivity gives ordinary Euler characteristic. The both-nonzero open locus has empty fixed locus and therefore compactly supported Euler characteristic zero.

value.rationale: Commuting varieties are classical singular algebraic varieties central to Lie theory and invariant theory. The theorem gives a global topological invariant for the full projectivized commuting variety in complete generality, without reductivity or irreducibility assumptions. The equality with the ambient projective Euler characteristic is structural because the commuting equations can impose substantial geometry while leaving this invariant unchanged. The stronger decomposition statement explains the equality: the entire both-nonzero locus has compactly supported Euler characteristic zero, and all Euler mass is concentrated on two canonical coordinate boundary components. This is a natural invariant of a standard family, not an arbitrary finite slice.
